from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Turbulence is a multi-scale energy cascade.", "Reynolds Number defines the transition to chaos.", "Predictable laminar flow breaks down."]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Chaos of the Coffee Cup", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a swirling [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cup.svg] model, label it 'Turbulent Flow' in #FF00FF
        cup = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cup.svg", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(cup, 'D4', scale_factor=0.6)
        label1 = Text("Turbulent Flow", font_size=24, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(label1, 'B4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(cup), Write(label1))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Fade out the cup, show a grid of velocity vectors in #00FFFF
        self.play(FadeOut(cup), FadeOut(label1))
        grid = VGroup(*[Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.3, color=WHITE).shift(i*RIGHT*0.5 + j*UP*0.5) for i in range(-2, 3) for j in range(-2, 3)])
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(grid))
        self.play(grid.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show small [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coffee.svg] eddies emerging, highlight them in #FFFF00
        eddies = VGroup(*[SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coffee.svg", color="#FFFF00").scale(0.3).move_to(self.grid['C3'] + np.array([0.2*i, 0.2*j, 0])) for i in range(-1, 2) for j in range(-1, 2)])
        self.play(FadeIn(eddies))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Navier-Stokes equations govern fluid motion.",
            "Inertia and viscosity compete.",
            "Scaling laws help describe complex flows."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Prerequisites: The Navier-Stokes Language", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        eq = MathTex(r"\frac{\partial \mathbf{u}}{\partial t} + (\mathbf{u} \cdot \nabla)\mathbf{u} = -\frac{1}{\rho}\nabla p + \nu \nabla^2 \mathbf{u}")
        div = MathTex(r"\nabla \cdot \mathbf{u} = 0")
        grad_p = MathTex(r"-\frac{1}{\rho}\nabla p")
        
        # Asset mobjects
        fluid_icon_1 = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fluid.svg")
        fluid_icon_2 = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fluid.svg")
        
        self.place_in_area(eq, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.75)
        self.place_at_grid(div, 'D2', scale_factor=0.75)
        self.place_at_grid(grad_p, 'E2', scale_factor=0.75)
        
        self.place_at_grid(fluid_icon_1, 'A2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(fluid_icon_2, 'F2', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Hide initially
        div.set_opacity(0)
        grad_p.set_opacity(0)
        fluid_icon_1.set_opacity(0)
        fluid_icon_2.set_opacity(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(eq), FadeIn(fluid_icon_1))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        div.set_opacity(1)
        self.play(FadeIn(div))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        grad_p.set_opacity(1)
        self.play(FadeIn(grad_p), FadeIn(fluid_icon_2))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Kolmogorov Constants and Scaling Laws", [
            "Energy follows a -5/3 power law.",
            "Kolmogorov constant K universalizes energy spectra.",
            "Large eddies cascade into smaller ones.",
            "Spectral density reveals turbulence structure.",
            "The inertial subrange shows universal scaling."
        ])
        
        # Define elements
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.5)
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 5 * (x + 0.1)**(-0.5), x_range=[0.5, 5], color=BLUE)
        inertial_bar = Rectangle(height=0.5, width=2, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        epsilon = MathTex(r"\\epsilon", color=RED).scale(1.5)
        
        # Assets
        turbine = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/turbine.svg")
        vortex = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vortex.svg")

        # Place elements
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(inertial_bar, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(epsilon, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(turbine, 'A5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(vortex, 'E2', scale_factor=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE), Create(curve), FadeIn(turbine))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), FadeIn(vortex))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW), Create(inertial_bar))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Viscosity eventually dissipates kinetic energy.", "Kolmogorov length scale limits eddy size.", "Structure breaks down into heat."]
        self.setup_layout("The Kolmogorov Length Scale", lecture_lines)
        
        # Formula for Kolmogorov length scale
        formula = MathTex(r"\eta = \left( \frac{\nu^3}{\epsilon} \right)^{1/4}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B1', 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Visualize Eddies
        eddies = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE, stroke_width=2),
            Circle(radius=0.75, color=BLUE, stroke_width=2),
            Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE, stroke_width=2),
            Circle(radius=0.1, color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        # Add heat icon
        heat_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/heat.svg", color=RED)
        heat_icon.next_to(eddies[3], RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        eddies.add(heat_icon)
        
        self.place_at_grid(eddies, 'E5', scale_factor=0.45)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(eddies[0:3]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(eddies[3]), FadeIn(heat_icon))
        self.play(Indicate(eddies[3]))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Constants enable efficient engineering models.",
            "Simulations bypass molecular-scale complexity.",
            "Dissipation dictates natural system behavior."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Real-World Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual elements

outline.topic: Fundamental Constants and Mathematical Structure in Turbulence
outline.target_audience: Advanced Undergraduate Physics or Engineering Students

sections.title: The Hook: The Chaos of the Coffee Cup
sections.content: Introduce turbulence as a multi-scale energy cascade. Define the transition from laminar flow to turbulence using the Reynolds Number (Re) as the primary dimensionless constant, signaling the breakdown of predictable flow.
sections.example: Visualizing a drop of milk swirling into a coffee cup: from a smooth stream (low Re) to complex, chaotic eddies (high Re).

sections.title: Mathematical Prerequisites: The Navier-Stokes Language
sections.content: Briefly review the Navier-Stokes equations, focusing on the competition between inertial forces and viscous forces. Introduce the concept of scaling laws before diving into Kolmogorov's theory.
sections.example: A 'Tug-of-War' animation: Inertia (The 'Bull') vs. Viscosity (The 'Anchor') determining the fate of a fluid parcel.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Constants and Scaling Laws
sections.content: Explain the -5/3 power law in the inertial subrange. Define the Kolmogorov constant (K ≈ 1.5) and explain how it universalizes the energy spectrum regardless of the fluid type.
sections.example: A graphical overlay showing a log-log plot of Energy vs. Wavenumber (k), illustrating the 'steep slope' where large eddies break down into smaller ones.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Length Scale: The End of the Cascade
sections.content: Describe the dissipation range where kinetic energy is finally converted to heat by viscosity. Introduce the Kolmogorov length scale (η) as the fundamental mathematical limit of turbulence structure.
sections.example: An animation of a 'Whirlpool Chain': Giant vortex structures shrinking until they become tiny, heat-generating friction points controlled by η.

sections.title: Synthesis and Real-World Application
sections.content: Summarize how these constants allow engineers to model complex systems without simulating every atom. Connect the theory back to the importance of dissipation in natural systems.
sections.example: A blue whale swimming: High-speed CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) simulations using these constants to predict the drag force on the whale's tail flukes during a dive.
